entries.test: Whether big tech executives publicly criticised or lobbied against the EU AI Act's political agreement in the days after it was reached in December 2023.
entries.note: 'Doing their best' is loose wording, but the plain reading is public opposition after the deal. The proposition leaves out 'aren't happy', which does not change the core claim.

Calling it a 'lie' asserts that LeCun knew it was false, and public evidence cannot show what he knew. 'Pushing hardest' is a ranking with no plain measure; the factual core is handled in the next three claims.

entries.test: The legislative history of the EU AI Act, showing when provisions on general-purpose AI or foundation models first entered the negotiating texts.
entries.note: This is settled together with the date claimed in the next claim.

entries.test: The dates of Council compromise texts, such as the Slovenian presidency text of November 2021 and the French presidency text of May 2022, showing when general-purpose AI first appeared.
entries.note: The Slovenian presidency's November 2021 compromise text may already have mentioned general-purpose AI, which would make 'first' false.

entries.test: Whether the first general-purpose AI provisions in AI Act negotiating texts came from the French Council presidency, or from an earlier presidency or EU institution.
entries.note: 'French government' here means France's presidency of the EU Council in the first half of 2022.
